Subject: Discovery recap — data privacy & logging requirements (FinTechCorp)

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid conversation. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps. Please let me know if I've missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Sensitive PII (names, SSNs, payment metadata) is being sent to multiple third-party NLP services today and the security team is concerned about exposure and auditability.
- Need strict retention controls and the ability to redact or transform PII before it is persisted.
- Strong requirement for immutable audit logs for requests and responses for regulatory audits.
- Desire to avoid vendor lock-in: ability to pin and export logs and transcripts for internal review.

Current stack / integration notes:
- Front-end collects customer messages and sends to a middleware service (in-house) that calls vendor inference APIs.
- You currently have a tokenization/redaction step, but it’s inconsistent and performed client-side only for some flows.
- Primary workloads: conversational QA and post-call summarization; peak concurrency ~150 qps.

Success criteria for POC / evaluation:
- Demonstrable redaction workflow covering field-level PII redaction or client-side tokenization.
- Configurable retention policies (per-route): options for 30/90/365 days and on-demand purge.
- Audit logs with exportable events and at least 13 months retention (or clear export path).
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and an architecture walkthrough for your security team.

What we can provide / next steps from Redwood:
- Attached: high-level SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) and a suggested retention/retention-mapping spreadsheet (data-retention-table.xlsx).
- Redwood supports both client-side tokenization and server-side redaction (we can discuss tradeoffs in the security deep-dive).
- Audit logs: request/response metadata and per-request routing traces are available; long-term retention (13+ months) available as an add-on.

Proposed next steps:
1) Security deep-dive (30–45m) — proposed slots next Tue/Wed afternoon PT; Priya, which day works best?
2) Provide a short POC plan: we’ll ship a small integration example that demonstrates redaction + audit log export.
3) Internal pricing / contract conversation pending after security sign-off.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call with your infra/security team and Rishi (copied) for the technical walkthrough.

Best,

Thanks — a few security items to call out before the deep-dive so Redwood can prepare concrete answers / artifacts: 

1) Audit logs: we need immutable, tamper-evident logs for all inference requests and routing events. Exportable in JSON/NDJSON. Retention requirement: minimum 13 months; preferred 24 months for some regulated lines. Please indicate whether logs are stored encrypted-at-rest and whether we can push logs to our SIEM (Splunk).

2) Redaction: for certain fields (SSN, account numbers, payment tokens) we require redaction at ingest (before persistent storage). Client-side tokenization is preferred, but server-side redaction is acceptable if we can verify it occurs prior to write. We also need the ability to rehydrate/redact for debugging under strict controls.

3) Key management: we require KMS integration (customer-managed keys preferred) for encryption of stored artifacts.

4) Access controls / audit: RBAC that ties to our SSO, detailed per-user audit for who accessed logs or downloaded transcripts.

5) POC data: for the proof of concept, we can supply synthetically masked data. We will need example requests/response logs that demonstrate redaction behavior and a short guide for ingestion.

Please include any architecture diagrams and the SOC 2 evidence (or pointer to where we can access it under NDA).

— Priya

Sam / Priya — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together specific answers below and attached the SOC 2 summary. We can share the full Type II report once an NDA is in place (standard process).

Quick answers to the bullets: 
- SOC 2: summary attached (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). Full Type II available under NDA; we can route that through your security team.
- Field-level redaction: Redwood supports both approaches: (a) client-side tokenization (we provide a small SDK and example) and (b) server-side redaction policies you can configure per-route. For server-side redaction we can provide rule examples (regex, named-field mapping) and a verification report from the POC.
- Retention: per-route retention is configurable. Standard plans include 30/90/365; 13-month retention and 24-month retention are both supported via an add-on retention policy. We’ll include pricing options in the follow-up.
- Audit logs: request/response metadata and routing traces are stored encrypted-at-rest. Logs are exportable in NDJSON and we support pushing to S3 or a customer-managed Splunk forwarder for ingestion. Tamper-evidence is provided via signed log batches and export manifests.
- KMS / keys: support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) is available for private deployments and as an option for Dedicated plans.
- Data residency / routing: yes — per-route region pinning is supported and can be part of the POC config.

Next steps I propose:
1) Security deep-dive (45m) — proposed slots: Tue 2/16 10–10:45am PT or Wed 2/17 1–1:45pm PT. Please pick one and we’ll send a calendar invite.
2) POC plan: we’ll prepare a POC checklist and a small SDK example for client-side tokenization; estimate time to stand up: 1–2 weeks.
3) SOC2 NDA — I’ll have our compliance team send the NDA link if you confirm you want the full report.

I’ve CC’ed Rishi (technical lead) and Lauren (sales lead) to help with scheduling and the POC scoping. Rishi, Lauren — can you own the POC doc and calendar invite?
